summary: Chang, Chen and Mishiba prove Thakur's basis conjecture for multiple zeta values over the function field k = F_q(θ): for every weight w, the values ζ_A(s) with s in Thakur's index set I^T_w — tuples of weight w whose entries are at most q, the last one strictly less — form a k-basis of the space Z_w spanned by the MZVs of weight w. Since |I^T_w| = d'_w this gives Todd's dimension conjecture, the analogue of Zagier's conjecture. The proof switches from the MZVs to the special values Li_s(1) of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, which agree with ζ_A(s) on Thakur's index set by Carlitz's identity. On the generation side the authors introduce a formal weight-graded space H on the set of indices carrying the harmonic and q-shuffle products, with realisation maps to k and k_∞ that turn the stuffle and q-shuffle relations into formal identities, and an explicit rewriting operator U^• which preserves the realisations and, after finitely many iterations, pushes any index into Thakur's set; this reproves Ngo Dac's generating theorem effectively and, as a by-product, identifies all k-linear relations among MZVs of a given weight as generated by [s] − U^ζ(s). On the independence side they run the Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion on the period interpretation of CMPL values, reduce a linear relation to a solution of an explicit system of Frobenius difference equations indexed by initial segments, and compute that the solution space of that system has dimension 1 when (q − 1) divides the weight and 0 otherwise, which forces the relation to be trivial. The atlas plans the objects this is built on — the Carlitz module, its period, Anderson t-modules and effective t-motives, Carlitz zeta values and Papanikolas's difference-Galois theory, all in the roadmap Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values — but nothing beyond depth one: no multiple zeta values in characteristic p, no Carlitz polylogarithms, no q-shuffle algebra and no ABP criterion. The classical analogues (Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures) are planned at PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.9.

items.name: The polynomial ring, its fraction field and the completion at infinity
items.statement: A := F_q[θ] is the polynomial ring over a finite field with q = p^e elements, k its fraction field, |·|_∞ the normalised absolute value at the infinite place with |θ|_∞ = q, and k_∞ := F_q((1/θ)) the completion; A_+ denotes the monic polynomials of A, the analogue of the positive integers.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2 (Theorem 1.5 of the published version numbers statements by section)
items.note: Mathlib has polynomial rings over a finite field, the field of rational functions and Laurent series, with monic polynomials; the arithmetic package built on them (the absolute value at infinity, A_+ graded by degree) is not assembled anywhere.

items.name: The completed algebraic closure C_∞ and the algebraic closure of k in it
items.statement: An algebraic closure k̄_∞ of k_∞ is fixed, |·|_∞ is extended to it, C_∞ is the completion of k̄_∞ for |·|_∞, and k̄ denotes the algebraic closure of k inside C_∞.
items.note: The function-field analogue of C_p. FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.0 plans curves, fields and constants for global function fields and the DrinfeldModulesAndTModules roadmap works over C_∞ throughout (analytic uniformisation in DM.2, periods in DM.8), so the object is assumed there; no layer constructs it explicitly.

items.name: Thakur's multiple zeta values
items.statement: For an r-tuple of positive integers s = (s_1, …, s_r), ζ_A(s) := Σ 1/(a_1^{s_1} ⋯ a_r^{s_r}) ∈ k_∞, the sum being over a_1, …, a_r ∈ A_+ with |a_1|_∞ > ⋯ > |a_r|_∞; the series converges because |·|_∞ is non-archimedean, and Thakur proved it is non-vanishing. Its weight is wt(s) = Σ s_i and its depth dep(s) = r. For r = 1 these are the Carlitz zeta values.
items.note: The central object of the paper. DM.6 plans Goss/Taelman L-values and requires the Carlitz module to recover its explicit zeta value, so the depth-one values are in the atlas's direction; the multiple values, their weight/depth grading and Thakur's non-vanishing theorem are not planned.

items.name: Carlitz zeta values and the Carlitz module
items.statement: The depth-one values ζ_A(s) = Σ_{a ∈ A_+} a^{-s} are the Carlitz zeta values, attached to the Carlitz module C : t ↦ θ + τ, whose exponential, period π̃ and logarithm control them.
items.note: DM.0 constructs the Carlitz module as the rank-one example, DM.2 its analytic uniformisation and period, and DM.6 requires the explicit Carlitz zeta value and period normalisation.

items.name: The algebra of multiple zeta values and Chang's descent theorem
items.statement: Thakur's q-shuffle relations express a product of two MZVs as an F_p-linear combination of MZVs of the same weight, so the k-vector space Z spanned by all MZVs is an algebra; and by the first author's theorem every k̄-linear relation among MZVs comes from k-linear relations among MZVs of the same weight. Hence determining dim_k Z_w is the central problem.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2 (after Thakur and Chang)
items.note: The structural facts that make the dimension question well posed; neither the q-shuffle algebra nor the descent from k̄ to k is planned in the atlas.

items.name: Classical multiple zeta values, Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures
items.statement: For w ≥ 2 let 𝔷_w be the Q-vector space spanned by the real MZVs of weight w, and set d_0 = 1, d_1 = 0, d_2 = 1 and d_w = d_{w-2} + d_{w-3}. Zagier's conjecture asserts dim_Q 𝔷_w = d_w (the upper bound is a theorem of Terasoma and Goncharov), and Hoffman's basis conjecture asserts that {ζ(s) : s admissible with all s_i ∈ {2,3}, wt(s) = w} is a basis of 𝔷_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Conjectures 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 (published: Conjectures 1.1 and 1.2)
items.note: PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results', which is where Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures live.

items.name: Todd's dimension conjecture
items.statement: For a positive integer w let Z_w be the k-vector space spanned by the MZVs of weight w, and define d'_w = 2^{w-1} for 1 ≤ w < q, d'_q = 2^{q-1} − 1, and d'_w = Σ_{i=1}^{q} d'_{w-i} for w > q. Then dim_k Z_w = d'_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Conjecture 1.2.2 (published: Conjecture 1.3; after Todd's numerical computations)
items.note: The function-field analogue of Zagier's conjecture; proved in this paper as a consequence of Thakur's basis conjecture.

items.name: Thakur's basis conjecture
items.statement: For a positive integer w let I^T_w be the set of tuples s = (s_1, …, s_r) of positive integers with wt(s) = w, s_i ≤ q for 1 ≤ i ≤ r − 1 and s_r < q. Then B^T_w := {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a basis of the k-vector space Z_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Conjecture 1.2.3 (published: Conjecture 1.4; after Thakur)
items.note: The function-field analogue of Hoffman's basis conjecture, and the main theorem of the paper; |I^T_w| = d'_w, so it implies Todd's conjecture.

items.name: The main theorem
items.statement: For every positive integer w, Thakur's basis conjecture holds; consequently Todd's dimension conjecture holds.
items.note: The paper's main result. Its proof has two halves: a generation half, which makes the candidate set span, and a linear-independence half through the ABP criterion.

items.name: Ngo Dac's upper bound
items.statement: For each w ≥ 1 the set B^T_w is a generating set of the k-vector space Z_w, so dim_k Z_w ≤ d'_w. The present paper reproves this in Corollary 3.2.5, in a form that also gives a generating set for the space spanned by the values Li_s(1).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Remark 1.2.5 (published: Remark 1.6; after Ngo Dac)
items.note: The half of the conjecture that was known; the paper's contribution on this side is a concrete and effective algorithm rather than a new bound.

items.name: Descent of the basis to k̄
items.statement: Since k-linear independence of MZVs implies k̄-linear independence, for each positive integer w the set B^T_w is also a basis for the k̄-vector space spanned by the MZVs of weight w.
items.note: Uses the first author's theorem quoted above.

items.name: An upper bound for v-adic multiple zeta values
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of k and, for a positive integer w, let Z_{v,w} be the k̄-vector space spanned by the v-adic MZVs of weight w. Then dim_k Z_{v,w} ≤ d'_w − d'_{w-(q-1)}, where d'_0 = 1 and d'_n = 0 for n < 0.
items.note: A consequence for the v-adic MZVs of Chang–Mishiba; the v-adic theory is not in the atlas either.

items.name: The parallel work on alternating multiple zeta values
items.statement: Independently and at the same time, Im, Kim, Le, Ngo Dac and Pham proved the corresponding results for alternating MZVs, by studying the k-vector space spanned by the values Li_s(γ_1, …, γ_r) with s ∈ I^T_w and γ_i ∈ F_{q^{q-1}}^×; the primary methods, rooted in Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas, Chang, Todd, Chang–Papanikolas–Yu and Ngo Dac, are the same, with different presentations.
items.note: Recorded because the two papers together fix the state of the art, and because the atlas will want both in the same roadmap.

items.name: Indices and the graded vector space of indices
items.statement: An index is the empty tuple ∅ or an r-tuple of positive integers, with dep(∅) = wt(∅) = 0, dep(s) = r and wt(s) = Σ s_i; I = ⊔_{r≥0} Z_{≥1}^r is the set of indices, with subsets I_w (weight w), I_{>0}, I^T_w (s_i ≤ q for i < r and s_r < q) and IND_w (q ∤ s_i for all i), and I^T_0 = IND_0 = {∅}. H = ⊕_{w≥0} H_w is the k-vector space with basis I graded by weight, [s] the generator attached to s, and Supp(P) the set of indices with nonzero coefficient in P.
items.note: The formal combinatorial framework in which both products and both realisations are defined; nothing analogous is planned in the atlas.

items.name: Thakur's and Ngo Dac's index sets have the same size
items.statement: For each weight w ≥ 0 there is a bijection between IND_w and I^T_w, given by (m_1 q + n_1, …, m_r q + n_r) ↔ (q^{{m_1}}, n_1, …, q^{{m_r}}, n_r) with m_i ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ n_i ≤ q − 1; hence |IND_w| = |I^T_w|.
items.note: The combinatorial identity that lets the linear independence proved for one index set be transported to Thakur's basis.

items.name: Concatenation and the multilinear bracket
items.statement: For indices s_1, …, s_ℓ, (s_1, …, s_ℓ) denotes their concatenation; for a non-empty index s = (s_1, …, s_r) one writes s_+ = (s_1, …, s_{r-1}) and s_- = (s_2, …, s_r). The k-multilinear map [−, …, −] : H^{⊕ℓ} → H is defined on indices by concatenation, so that [s, 0] = 0 while [s, ∅] ≠ 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 2.1.4 and Remark 2.1.5 (published: Definition 2.2 and Remark 2.3)
items.note: The bookkeeping operations on H used in every formula of Sections 2 and 3.

items.name: Carlitz polylogarithms and Carlitz multiple polylogarithms
items.statement: With L_0 = 1 and L_d = (θ − θ^q) ⋯ (θ − θ^{q^d}), the Carlitz logarithm is log_C(z) = Σ_{d≥0} z^{q^d}/L_d, the n-th Carlitz polylogarithm of Anderson–Thakur is Li_n(z) = Σ_{d≥0} z^{q^d}/L_d^n, and for an index s of positive depth the s-th Carlitz multiple polylogarithm (CMPL) is Li_s(z_1, …, z_r) = Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0} z_1^{q^{d_1}} ⋯ z_r^{q^{d_r}} / (L_{d_1}^{s_1} ⋯ L_{d_r}^{s_r}).
items.note: DM.8 plans Carlitz logarithms and their algebraic independence after Papanikolas; the polylogarithms of Anderson–Thakur and their multiple version, introduced by the first author, are the objects this paper actually works with and are not planned.

items.name: Power sums and the three realisation maps
items.statement: For s ≥ 1 and d ≥ 0 put S^{Li}_d(s) := 1/L_d^s and S^ζ_d(s) := Σ_{a ∈ A_{+,d}} 1/a^s, where A_{+,d} is the set of monic polynomials of degree d. For • ∈ {Li, ζ} the k-linear maps 𝔏^•_d, 𝔏^•_{<d} : H → k and 𝔏^• : H → k_∞ are defined by the corresponding sums over d = d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0, over d > d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0 and over d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0, with the conventions on ∅; they satisfy 𝔏^•_d = 𝔏^•_{<d+1} − 𝔏^•_{<d}, 𝔏^• = lim_d 𝔏^•_{<d}, 𝔏^{Li}(s) = Li_s(1) and 𝔏^ζ(s) = ζ_A(s).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 2.2.2 with the identities after it (published: Definition 2.4)
items.note: The formal separation of the two realisations — CMPL values and MZVs — on the same space of indices, which is what lets one algorithm serve both.

items.name: Carlitz's identity and the agreement of the two realisations
items.statement: For 1 ≤ s ≤ q and d ≥ 0 one has 1/L_d^s = Σ_{a ∈ A_{+,d}} 1/a^s (Carlitz); hence for an index s with 1 ≤ s_i ≤ q for all i one has 𝔏^{Li}_d(s) = 𝔏^ζ_d(s), 𝔏^{Li}_{<d}(s) = 𝔏^ζ_{<d}(s) and Li_s(1) = ζ_A(s).
items.note: The identity that makes Thakur's basis a set of CMPL values, which is what the linear independence argument can handle.

items.name: The harmonic product
items.statement: The harmonic product * = *^{Li} is the k-bilinear map H × H → H with [∅] * P = P * [∅] = P and [s] * [n] = [s_1, s_- * n] + [n_1, s * n_-] + [s_1 + n_1, s_- * n_-]; one sets D^{Li}_{s,n} := 0.
items.note: The stuffle product, which the CMPL realisation preserves.

items.name: Chen's formula and the q-shuffle product
items.statement: H.-J. Chen proved 𝔏^ζ_d(s)𝔏^ζ_d(n) = 𝔏^ζ_d(s+n) + Σ_{j=1}^{s+n-1} Δ^{[j]}_{s,n} 𝔏^ζ_d(s+n−j, j), where Δ^{[j]}_{s,n} = (−1)^{s-1}C(j−1, s−1) + (−1)^{n-1}C(j−1, n−1) if (q−1) | j and 1 ≤ j < s + n, and 0 otherwise. The q-shuffle product *^ζ on H is the k-bilinear map with [∅] *^ζ P = P and [s] *^ζ [n] = [s_1, s_- *^ζ n] + [n_1, s *^ζ n_-] + [s_1 + n_1, s_- *^ζ n_-] + D^ζ_{s,n}, where D^ζ_{s,n} = Σ_{j=1}^{s_1+n_1-1} Δ^{[j]}_{s_1,n_1} [s_1 + n_1 − j, (j) *^ζ (s_- *^ζ n_-)]; both products preserve the weight grading.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 2.3, equations (2.3.2)–(2.3.4) (after H.-J. Chen and Thakur)
items.note: The function-field shuffle: unlike the classical case it is not a shuffle of words, and the correction term D^ζ is what makes the combinatorics of Section 3 delicate.

items.name: Vanishing of the correction term in low weight
items.statement: If s + n ≤ q then Δ^{[j]}_{s,n} = 0 for all j; hence for indices s, n of positive depth with s_1 + n_1 ≤ q one has D^ζ_{s,n} = 0.
items.note: The reason Thakur's index set, where the entries are ≤ q, is so well behaved.

items.name: The realisations are algebra maps
items.note: The formal statement that the stuffle relations for CMPLs and the q-shuffle relations for MZVs are realisations of the two products on H.

items.name: The box-plus operator
items.statement: ⊞ : H^{⊕2} → H is the k-linear map with ∅ ⊞ P = P ⊞ ∅ = 0 and s ⊞ n := (s_+, s_r + n_1, n_-) for indices s = (s_+, s_r) and n = (n_1, n_-) of positive depth; in depth one, (s) ⊞ (n) = [s + n], and (n) ⊞ P ≠ [n] + P in general.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 3.1.1 and Remark 3.1.2 (published: Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2)
items.note: The operation that glues the last entry of one index to the first entry of another.

items.name: The Thakur decomposition of an index
items.statement: Every index is written uniquely as s = (s^T, q^{{m}}, s') with s^T ∈ I^T, m ≥ 0 and either s' = ∅ or s'_1 > q; when s' ≠ ∅ one sets s'' := (s'_1 − q, s'_-). For example s = (q−1, q, q, q+1, 1) has s^T = (q−1), m = 2, s' = (q+1, 1) and s'' = (1, 1).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 3.1, equations (3.1.1)–(3.1.2) and Example 3.1.5 (published: Example 3.3)
items.note: The decomposition that measures how far an index is from Thakur's set and drives the induction in Theorem 3.2.4.

items.name: The operators α_q and U^•
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} set α^•_q(P) := [1, (q−1) *^• P], with α^{•,0}_q the identity and α^{•,m}_q its m-th iterate. The k-linear map U^• : H → H is defined on an index s with decomposition (s^T, q^{{m}}, s') by U^•(s) = −[s^T, q^{{m+1}}, s''] + L_1^{m+1}[s^T, α^{•,m+1}_q(s'')] + L_1^{m+1}(s^T ⊞ α^{•,m+1}_q(s'')) − [s^T, q^{{m}}, D^•_{q,s''}] when s' ≠ ∅, and by U^•(s) = L_1^m[s^T, α^{•,m}_q(∅)] + L_1^m(s^T ⊞ α^{•,m}_q(∅)) when s' = ∅. It preserves the weight grading, and U^•(s) = s for s ∈ I^T.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 3.2.2 with Remark 3.2.3 (published: Definition 3.4 and Remark 3.5)
items.note: The explicit rewriting operator; making it explicit, rather than an existence statement, is one of the paper's contributions over earlier work.

items.name: The rewriting algorithm
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and every P ∈ H: (1) 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P); (2) there is an explicit integer e ≥ 0 with Supp((U^•)^e(P)) ⊂ I^T.
items.note: The engine of the generation half: iterating U^• rewrites any index into Thakur's set without changing the value. Its proof occupies the appendix.

items.name: Generating sets in both realisations
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and w ≥ 0, let Z^•_w be the k-vector space spanned by the values 𝔏^•(s) for s ∈ I_w. Then {𝔏^•(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a generating set of Z^•_w; in particular Z^{Li}_w = Z^ζ_w = Z_w.
items.note: Reproves Ngo Dac's generation theorem and, at the same time, identifies the space of MZVs of weight w with the space of CMPL values of weight w.

items.name: The second generating set
items.statement: The k-vector space Z_w is spanned by the values Li_s(1) for s ∈ IND_w.
items.note: The generating set on which the linear independence argument is run, chosen because IND_w is the index set adapted to the Frobenius difference equations.

items.name: Frobenius twisting, the Tate algebra and the ring of entire functions
items.statement: For a new variable t and f = Σ a_i t^i ∈ C_∞((t)) the n-fold Frobenius twist is f^{(n)} := Σ a_i^{q^n} t^i, extended entrywise to matrices; τ^n is an automorphism of C_∞((t)) stabilising C_∞[[t]], the Tate algebra T of power series converging on |t|_∞ ≤ 1, the polynomial rings C_∞[t] and k̄[t] and the fields C_∞(t) and k̄(t), and σ := τ^{-1}. One has T^τ = k̄[t]^τ = F_q[t] = T^σ = k̄[t]^σ and k̄(t)^τ = F_q(t) = k̄(t)^σ. Following ABP, E is the subring of C_∞[[t]] of power series with algebraic coefficients a_i ∈ k̄ such that |a_i|_∞^{1/i} → 0 and [k_∞(a_0, a_1, …) : k_∞] < ∞; such series converge on all of C_∞ and E^τ = F_q[t] = E^σ.
items.note: The standard Frobenius-difference setting of characteristic-p transcendence theory. DM.4 and DM.8 work with τ-actions on t-motives and with rigid analytic triviality, so this setting belongs to that roadmap; the Tate algebra T and the ABP ring E are not constructed in the atlas (the Tate algebra planned in DM.2 is the one of analytic uniformisation).

items.name: The Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion
items.statement: Let Φ ∈ Mat_ℓ(k̄[t]) be such that det Φ vanishes, if at all, only at t = θ, and let ψ ∈ Mat_{ℓ×1}(E) satisfy ψ^{(-1)} = Φψ. If ρ ∈ Mat_{1×ℓ}(k̄) satisfies ρψ(θ) = 0, then there is 𝒫 ∈ Mat_{1×ℓ}(k̄[t]) with 𝒫ψ = 0 and 𝒫(θ) = ρ.
items.note: The linear independence criterion on which all characteristic-p transcendence results of this kind rest. DM.8 plans Papanikolas's Tannakian difference-Galois theory, which is built on this criterion and its specialisation/lifting statements, so the criterion belongs inside that layer; it is not stated there.

items.name: Initial segments, the coefficient ring R and the Frobenius system (E_M)
items.statement: For an index s = (s_1, …, s_r), 𝔦(s) := {∅, (s_1), (s_1, s_2), …, s} and 𝔦(M) := ∪_{s ∈ M} 𝔦(s); R := {f/g : f ∈ k̄[t], g ∈ F_q[t] \ {0}} ⊂ k̄(t). For w ≥ 0 and ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w the system (E_M) of Frobenius equations is ε_s^{(1)} = ε_s (t − θ)^{w − wt(s)} + Σ_{s' > 0, (s, s') ∈ 𝔦(M)} ε_{(s,s')} (t − θ)^{w − wt(s)} for s ∈ 𝔦(M), with (ε_s) ∈ R^{𝔦(M)}. For w = 0 it reduces to ε_∅^{(1)} = ε_∅.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 4.2, equation (E_M), with Remark 4.2.1 (published: Remark 4.2)
items.note: The system is the case Q_i = 1 of Chang–Papanikolas–Yu's equations, written with subscripts indexed by initial segments following Ngo Dac.

items.name: Solutions of a twisted linear equation are polynomial
items.statement: Let F = Σ_{i=0}^n f_i t^i and G lie in A[t] with n = deg_t F ≥ 1 and f_n ∈ F_q^×. If ε ∈ R satisfies ε^{(1)} = εF + G, then ε ∈ F_q(t)[θ].
items.note: The rationality step: it removes denominators and puts the solutions in a polynomial ring in θ over F_q(t).

items.name: Degree bound for the solutions
items.statement: Let w ≥ 0 and ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w. If (ε_s)_{s ∈ 𝔦(M)} ∈ R^{𝔦(M)} satisfies (E_M), then ε_s ∈ F_q(t)[θ] and deg_θ ε_s ≤ (w − wt(s))/(q − 1) for each s ∈ 𝔦(M).
items.note: The degree bound that makes the solution space finite dimensional and is the source of the divisibility condition by q − 1.

items.name: The index set IND°_w and the system (E_w)
items.statement: IND°_w := {∅} for w = 0 and, for w > 0, the set of (s_1, …, s_r) ∈ IND_w with s_2, …, s_r divisible by q − 1; (E_w) is the system (E_M) for M = IND°_w, and X_w denotes its set of R-valued solutions, an F_q(t)-vector subspace of R^{𝔦(IND°_w)} since f^{(1)} = f for f ∈ F_q(t).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 4.3, equation (4.3.1), Definition 4.3.3 and Remark 4.3.4 (published: Definition 4.6 and Remark 4.7)
items.note: The description of IND°_w comes from the simultaneously Eulerian phenomenon of Chang–Papanikolas–Yu, first observed by Lara Rodríguez and Thakur.

items.name: Worked examples of the Frobenius system
items.statement: For w = 0 the system (E_w) is the single equation ε_∅^{(1)} = ε_∅; for w = q, IND°_q = {(1, q−1)} and 𝔦(IND°_q) = {∅, (1), (1, q−1)} give three equations; for w = 2q − 2 with q ≥ 3, IND°_{2q-2} = {(q−1, q−1), (2q−2)} gives four equations, written out explicitly in the paper.
items.note: The acceptance examples for any implementation of the system.

items.name: The dimension of the solution space
items.statement: For every w ≥ 0, dim_{F_q(t)} X_w = 1 if (q − 1) | w and 0 otherwise. When w = ℓ(q − 1) one may choose a generator (η_{ℓ;s}) with η_{ℓ;∅} = Σ_{i=0}^{ℓ} b_{ℓi}(t − θ)^i, where b_{ℓi} ∈ T F_p[T]_{(T)} for 0 ≤ i < ℓ and b_{ℓℓ} = 1, with T := t − t^q and F_p[T]_{(T)} the localisation of F_p[T] at (T).
items.note: The key computation of Section 4 and the reason the answer depends only on the congruence of w modulo q − 1.

items.name: Eulerian values
items.statement: A value is Eulerian when it is a k-multiple of a power of the Carlitz period π̃; concretely, Li_P(1) = Σ_s a_s Li_s(1) is Eulerian of weight w when it lies in k · π̃^w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma 5.1.1 (published: Lemma 5.1), second hypothesis
items.note: The Carlitz period π̃ and its transcendence belong to DM.2 and DM.8; the notion of an Eulerian multiple zeta value, and the simultaneously Eulerian phenomenon that shapes IND°_w, are specific to this circle of ideas.

items.name: The key lemma
items.statement: Let w ≥ 0, ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w and P = Σ a_s[s] ∈ H with coefficients in k such that Supp(P) ⊂ M, Li_P(1) is Eulerian, and the values Li_s(1) for s ∈ 𝔦(M) ∩ I_ℓ are k-linearly independent for each 0 ≤ ℓ < w. Then: (1) for each s ∈ 𝔦(M), either Σ_{s' ∈ I_{w-wt(s)}} a_{(s,s')}Li_{s'}(1) = 0 or (q − 1) | (w − wt(s)); in particular, if the relevant values are linearly independent then Supp(P) ⊂ {(s_1, …, s_r) ∈ I_w : (q − 1) | s_2, …, s_r}; and (2) the system (E_M) has a solution (ε_s) ∈ F_q(t)[θ]^{𝔦(M)} with ε_s = a_s|_{θ = t} for each s ∈ M.
items.note: The bridge from a linear relation among CMPL values to a solution of the Frobenius system, obtained from the ABP criterion together with the induction hypothesis.

items.name: Linear independence of the CMPL values
items.statement: For each w ≥ 0 the values Li_s(1) with s ∈ IND_w form a basis of Z_w.
items.note: The linear independence half of the main theorem, proved by induction on w: a relation gives a solution of (E_w) by the key lemma, and Theorem 4.3.5 forces it to vanish.

items.name: Proof of the main theorem
items.statement: Since |I^T_w| = |IND_w| (Proposition 2.1.1) and B^T_w generates Z_w (Corollary 3.2.5), while {Li_s(1) : s ∈ IND_w} is a basis of Z_w (Theorem 5.2.1), the set B^T_w is a k-basis of Z_w; hence dim_k Z_w = |I^T_w| = d'_w, which is Todd's conjecture.
items.note: The assembly of the two halves.

items.name: All linear relations among multiple zeta values
items.statement: Let w be a positive integer. All k-linear relations among the MZVs of weight w are generated by the relations [s] − U^ζ(s) for s ∈ I_w \ I^T_w: writing 𝔏^ζ_w : H_w ↠ Z_w for the realisation and R_w := Span_k{[s] − U^ζ(s) : s ∈ I_w \ I^T_w}, one has Ker 𝔏^ζ_w = R_w, and Ker 𝔏^ζ = ⊕_{w ∈ N} R_w.
items.note: The effective description of the ideal of relations; it is the mechanism the authors advertise as going beyond earlier work, and it answers a shuffle-version of Todd's Conjecture 5.1.

items.name: Depth bounds for the products
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and indices s, n, every u ∈ Supp(s *^• n) satisfies max{dep(s), dep(n)} ≤ dep(u) ≤ dep(s) + dep(n).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Proposition A.1.1 (published: Proposition A.1)
items.note: The first of the combinatorial estimates that make the rewriting algorithm terminate.

items.name: Depth bounds for the correction terms and for α_q
items.statement: For non-empty indices s, n every u ∈ Supp(D^ζ_{s,n}) satisfies max{dep(s), dep(n)} ≤ dep(u) ≤ dep(s) + dep(n); and for m ≥ 0 every u ∈ Supp(α^{•,m}_q(s)) satisfies dep(u) ≥ 1 + m if s = ∅ and m ≥ 1, dep(u) ≥ dep(s) + m otherwise, and dep(u) ≤ dep(s) + 2m.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Corollary A.1.2 (published: Corollary A.2)
items.note: The bounds used to control the iterates of U^•.

items.name: Binary relations and the spaces P^•_w
items.statement: A binary relation of weight w is a pair (P, Q) of elements of H such that 𝔏^•_d(P) + 𝔏^•_{d+1}(Q) = 0 for every d ∈ Z; these form the space P^•_w. Thakur's identity 𝔏^ζ_d(q) − L_1 𝔏^ζ_{d+1}(1, q−1) = 0 gives the basic relation R_1 = ([q], −L_1[1, q−1]) ∈ P^•_q, valid for both realisations by Carlitz's identity.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section A.2 with Example A.2.3 (published: Example A.3)
items.note: The formal calculus of relations between truncated sums at consecutive degrees, from which the identity 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P) is assembled.

items.name: Operations on binary relations
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ}, every index s of positive depth and integers m ≥ 0, w > 0, the maps B^•_s, C^•_s and BC^{•,m}_q satisfy B^•_s(P^•_w) ⊂ P^•_{w+wt(s)}, C^•_s(P^•_w) ⊂ P^•_{w+wt(s)} and BC^{•,m}_q(P^•_w) ⊂ P^•_{w+mq}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Proposition A.3.1 (published: Proposition A.4)
items.note: The maps that propagate a binary relation to higher weight, used to prove the first half of Theorem 3.2.4.

items.name: U^• preserves the realisations
items.statement: For each P ∈ H one has 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem A.3.2 (published: Theorem A.5; this is Theorem 3.2.4(1))
items.note: Proved by exhibiting the defining formula of U^• as a combination of binary relations.

items.name: Strict progress of the rewriting
items.statement: Let s ∈ I \ I^T. Then: (1) if n ∈ Supp(U^•_1(s)) then dep(n) > dep(s); (2) if n ∈ Supp(U^•_2(s)) then dep(n) ≥ dep(s) and Init(n) > Init(s) lexicographically; (3) if n ∈ Supp(U^•_3(s)) then dep(n) ≥ dep(s) > ℓ_1 := dep(Init(s)), Init(n) ≥ Init(s) and 1 ≤ n_{ℓ_1+1} < s_{ℓ_1+1}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma A.3.7 (published: Lemma A.6)
items.note: The termination argument: each of the three parts of U^• strictly increases a combinatorial measure.

items.name: Termination of the rewriting algorithm
items.statement: For each P ∈ H there exists e ≥ 0 with Supp((U^•)^e(P)) ⊂ I^T.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem A.3.8 (published: Theorem A.7; this is Theorem 3.2.4(2))
items.note: The second half of Theorem 3.2.4, and with it the effective algorithm expressing any MZV in Thakur's basis.

items.name: Switching from multiple zeta values to CMPL values
items.statement: The proof replaces the study of the MZVs by that of the special values Li_s(1) of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms: by the Anderson–Thakur interpolation formula and the first author's work every ζ_A(s) is a k-linear combination of CMPL values at integral points, and for s ∈ I^T_w one has the identity ζ_A(s) = Li_s(1). The argument then splits into a generation half (Corollary 3.2.5 and Theorem 3.2.6) and a linear-independence half (Theorem 5.2.1) run through the ABP criterion.
items.note: The organising idea of the paper; the Anderson–Thakur interpolation and the polynomials it rests on are inputs from the literature that the atlas does not cover.

items.name: The period interpretation of CMPL values
items.statement: The special values of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms have a period interpretation: there are matrices Φ̃ ∈ Mat(k̄[t]) and ψ̃ ∈ Mat(E) with ψ̃^{(-1)} = Φ̃ψ̃ satisfying the hypotheses of the ABP criterion, for which a linear relation among the Li_s(1) becomes a k-linear relation among the entries of ψ̃(θ); applying the argument of Chang–Papanikolas–Yu to it produces the system (E_w) of Frobenius difference equations.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.3, step (II-1) (after Chang, and Anderson–Thakur for MZVs)
items.note: This is the input the paper deliberately does not reprove ('we avoid many details in II-(1)'); any blueprint must plan it, since it is what connects the analytic values to the difference equations. It belongs with the t-motive machinery of DM.4 and DM.8.
